s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital renal and developmental disorder with multi-organ involvement and metabolic disturbances
salient_findings: Enlarged kidneys bilaterally with increased renal echogenicity
Severe metabolic acidosis and electrolyte imbalances
Abnormal liver enzymes and bile duct dilatation
key_facts: Prenatal ultrasound showed slightly enhanced parenchymal echoes and enlarged kidneys bilaterally
Born at term with normal birth parameters
Contracted pneumonia at 2 weeks
Admitted for shortness of breath and poor appetite at 3 weeks
Weight loss, dehydration, and hypotonia at 3 weeks
Required respiratory support through continuous positive airway pressure
Hypernatremia and involuntary eye movements at 4 weeks
Elevated serum creatinine, high plasma urea, hyperkalemia, and hyperchloremia
Severe metabolic acidosis with anemia
Elevated liver enzymes and thyroid-stimulating hormone
Dilatation of intrahepatic bile ducts in left liver lobe
Abnormal 24-h ambulatory EEG
Compound heterozygous variants in WDR19 and TG genes

shortlist.label: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Prenatal ultrasound showed enlarged kidneys bilaterally and increased renal echogenicity

shortlist.label: Nephronophthisis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum creatinine, high plasma urea, and hyperkalemia suggest chronic kidney disease

shortlist.label: Joubert Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Involuntary eye movements, developmental delay, and abnormal EEG suggest a neurodevelopmental disorder

shortlist.label: Cystinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes and thyroid-stimulating hormone, along with renal impairment, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Senior-Loken Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of renal disease, developmental delay, and eye abnormalities make this a plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The combination of renal abnormalities (enlarged kidneys and elevated serum creatinine), liver involvement (dilatation of intrahepatic bile ducts), developmental delays, and abnormal neurological findings (involuntary eye movements and abnormal EEG) are consistent with Joubert Syndrome, which is a disorder characterized by brain, kidney, and liver abnormalities. The presence of compound heterozygous variants in the WDR19 gene, which is associated with Joubert Syndrome, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
rejected.why: While the patient has renal abnormalities, the presence of liver and neurological findings are more suggestive of Joubert Syndrome.

rejected.label: Nephronophthisis
rejected.why: Nephronophthisis typically presents with renal failure and does not typically involve liver or neurological abnormalities to the extent seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Cystinosis
rejected.why: Cystinosis is characterized by the accumulation of cystine within cells, leading to renal failure and other systemic complications, but the presence of liver and neurological findings in this patient are more suggestive of Joubert Syndrome.

rejected.label: Senior-Loken Syndrome
rejected.why: Senior-Loken Syndrome is characterized by renal failure and retinal dystrophy, but the presence of liver and neurological findings in this patient are more suggestive of Joubert Syndrome.
